title: Home Medication Safety for Patients With Limited English Proficiency
summary: Build a safer home medication workflow using reconciliation, language support, teach-back, pharmacy coordination, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


It is a structured comparison of the medicines and products a patient actually uses at home with current clinical, discharge, pharmacy, and specialist records. An authorized clinician or pharmacist resolves discrepancies and creates the current plan.


###


Ask for prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, vitamins, supplements, inhalers, injections, patches, liquids, creams, eye drops, pill organizers, measuring devices, and any medication lists or instructions.


###


An aide should follow the plan of care and agency policy. The aide can observe and report a discrepancy, but medication decisions and plan changes belong to authorized clinicians or pharmacists.


###


Use qualified language support, then ask the patient or caregiver to explain the plan or demonstrate the approved task. Reteach and check again when the response differs from the current plan.


###


Evaluate language and dialect coverage, clinical terminology, audio reliability, quality monitoring, privacy and security, phone and telehealth access, documentation, document translation, downtime procedures, and escalation to another modality.
